what_happened: The the person running Athena ran `athena approve-work --yes` inside a shell command with a 5-minute limit. The command does not only approve the item. It goes on to run the approved job. The time limit killed the process while job 20261102-001719-1fva was in planning, so the job was left interrupted. No work was judged bad.
cause: Athena does not show what a command will do before it runs. A command named like an approval also starts a long job. It does not say how long the run will take, and it does not refuse to start in a foreground call that has a time limit. Safe use depends on the the person running Athena remembering which commands only change state and which run jobs. This is the same cause as the other mistakes where the the person running Athena acts on a command without seeing what it will act on, and Athena does not guard it.
prevention: Make approve-work only approve by default, so that running the job takes an explicit flag (for example --run). When it would run the job, it should print before starting that it will run the whole job and roughly how long that takes. It should also start the job as a tracked, detached run, or refuse to run in the foreground unless the the person running Athena confirms that no time limit applies. Add a short line to the the person running Athena guide naming which commands run jobs. A job that a kill interrupted should be shown as resumable, not as lost.
proposed_request: Change `athena approve-work` so it approves queue items and does not run the approved job unless the the person running Athena passes an explicit `--run` flag. Without the flag, it should record the approval, print the next command to run, and exit quickly. With `--run`, it should print one line before starting that the whole job will run and give the typical duration. Then it should start the job as a tracked, detached run that survives the end of the calling shell and prints how to follow its progress. Acceptance: (1) running approve-work without --run starts no job and leaves the item approved; (2) running it with --run starts the job detached, and killing the calling process does not stop the job; (3) the help text and the the person running Athena guide state which commands run jobs; (4) tests cover both modes. Do not change what approval means for items in other commands.
